hook: When a city started charging households for each bag of trash, landfill trash fell by about a third within a year. People did not stop shopping. They put more in the recycling bin, started composting food and yard waste, and bought less packaging. A small price changed a lot of habits.

figure.caption: The waste hierarchy: reduce first, then reuse, recycle and compost, then recover energy, and landfill last.

chain.cause: Products are designed with less material and people buy less (source reduction)
chain.effect: less waste is created at all
fewer new products must be made, saving materials and energy

chain.cause: Materials are recycled and food and yard waste is composted
chain.effect: less goes to landfills, less ore is mined, and less landfill methane forms

chain.cause: What remains can be burned for energy, and landfills capture their methane
chain.effect: some energy is recovered from waste that could not be avoided

ideas: The waste hierarchy: reduce, reuse, recycle and compost, recover energy, then landfill. The earlier steps save the most.
Source reduction means making less waste in the first place: less packaging, durable products, buying only what is needed.

Recycling saves resources and energy (aluminum about 95%) but costs money to collect and sort; some plastics have weak markets. Composting turns food and yard waste into humus and avoids landfill methane.
Other tools: landfill gas capture for electricity, e-waste recycling, and policies such as deposits, bag fees and pay-as-you-throw.

misconception.wrong: Recycling is the best thing you can do about waste.
misconception.right: Reducing and reusing come first, because they avoid making the waste at all. Recycling is better than landfilling, but it still uses energy to collect, sort and process materials.

summary: Waste is reduced by following the hierarchy: reduce first (less packaging, durable goods), then reuse, then recycle and compost, then recover energy, with landfilling last. Recycling saves materials and energy but has costs; composting turns food and yard waste into soil and avoids landfill methane. Policies such as pay-as-you-throw, bag fees and deposits shift behavior, and landfill gas can generate electricity.
